metadata.name: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
metadata.description: The NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) is a voluntary framework to help organizations that design, develop, deploy, or use AI systems manage the many risks of AI and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use of AI systems. Part 2 (the AI RMF Core) comprises four functions - GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE - each broken down into categories and subcategories that describe specific outcomes and actions for managing AI risk. GOVERN is a cross-cutting function infused throughout the other three. The framework is outcome-based and non-prescriptive.
metadata.source_organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
metadata.classification_reasoning: NIST AI 100-1 explicitly states the framework is voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, use-case agnostic, and outcome-focused rather than prescriptive. It is directed by the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283) but imposes no mandatory legal obligations of its own. Subcategories describe outcomes, not mandatory controls.
metadata.framework_purpose: To offer a resource to organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems to help manage the many risks of AI and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use of AI systems.
metadata.framework_scope: AI actors across the AI lifecycle - organizations and individuals of all sizes and sectors that play an active role in the AI system lifecycle, including those that design, develop, deploy, evaluate, acquire, operate, or use AI systems. The framework is non-sector-specific and use-case agnostic.
framework_objectives: Cultivate and implement a culture of AI risk management (GOVERN)
Establish and understand the context to frame risks related to an AI system (MAP)
Analyze, assess, benchmark, and monitor AI risk and related impacts (MEASURE)
Prioritize and act upon AI risks based on projected impact (MANAGE)

Enhance the trustworthiness of AI systems across characteristics: valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed
metadata.target_audience: AI actors across the lifecycle - including organizational management, senior leadership, boards, data scientists, ML engineers, developers, deployers, operators, TEVV experts, domain experts, human factors experts, impact assessors, procurement, governance and oversight roles, and legal/privacy governance
required_artifacts: AI risk management policies, processes, and procedures
TEVV test plans and result documentation
Risk register and risk treatment plans
Post-deployment monitoring plans and incident records
metadata.regulatory_authority: NIST (issuing body); directed by the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283). The framework is voluntary and law/regulation-agnostic.
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: None - the AI RMF is voluntary. It is intended to augment existing risk practices and should align with applicable laws, regulations, and norms, but the framework itself imposes no penalties.
adoption_approach: Institute the outcomes in the GOVERN function (governance structure, policies, roles, culture)
Apply MAP to establish context and identify risks; make an initial go/no-go decision
Apply MEASURE to analyze, assess, benchmark, and monitor identified risks using TEVV
Apply MANAGE to prioritize, respond to, and recover from risks based on projected impact
Use AI RMF Profiles (use-case, temporal current/target, cross-sectoral) to tailor implementation
Iterate across functions throughout the AI lifecycle as context, capabilities, and impacts evolve

levels: Subcategory (e.g., GOVERN 1.1, MAP 1.1) - the specific outcomes/actions

sections: GOVERN (Function) - A culture of risk management is cultivated and present
MAP (Function) - Context is recognized and risks related to context are identified
MEASURE (Function) - Identified risks are assessed, analyzed, or tracked
MANAGE (Function) - Risks are prioritized and acted upon based on a projected impact
document_structure.note_on_controls: The AI RMF Core describes OUTCOMES and actions (not a checklist or ordered steps). Subcategories are treated here as the framework's discrete requirements/controls. is_mandatory is set to false because the framework is explicitly voluntary and outcome-based.
